passage:
Elizabeth: you okay? you went silent after the meeting
Salma: he did it again. called my forecast "kindergarten work" in front of eleven people
Salma: two of them looked at their laps. nobody said anything
Elizabeth: I'm so sorry. That's not okay
Salma: I keep wondering if I really am that bad at this. my hands were shaking
Elizabeth: One weak forecast doesn't make it fair to belittle you in front of a room. You can be corrected without being humiliated
Salma: I typed the date and his exact words into my phone right after
Elizabeth: Good. Keep doing that. Would you talk to Ravi? He's been here ten years and people trust him. Then HR if it continues
Salma: Ravi first. Then HR
Elizabeth: I'll sit next to you in the next meeting. Walk at lunch?
Salma: yes. thanks for not saying it's just his style

qa.q: How many people were in the room when Salma's forecast was called kindergarten work?
qa.a: Eleven people were in the room.

qa.q: Why were Salma's hands shaking, and what doubt was Salma carrying?
qa.a: Salma was humiliated and shaken, and doubted being any good at the job.

qa.q: What has Salma done to keep a record, and what is planned next?
qa.a: Salma saved the date and the manager's exact words in a phone note, and plans to talk to Ravi first, then HR if it continues.

qa.q: Why might the two colleagues who looked at their laps have said nothing?
qa.a: They may have felt uncomfortable or worried about drawing the manager's attention, though the chat does not say.

grounding: A manager belittles a worker in a meeting; the worker feels humiliated, documents it, and turns to a trusted senior and HR.
